questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is I related to H if ‘B + R × I − T ÷ H’?
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’;
‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’;
‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and
‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’.
Based on the above, how is I related to H if ‘B + R × I − T ÷ H’?
questions.solution:
B is the mother of R, R is the wife of I, I is the brother of T and T is the father of H.

S, I is the Father’s brother of H.

questions.question: Six numbers 5, 3, 6, 7, 9 and 2 are written on different faces of a dice. Two positions of this dice are shown in the figure below. Find the number on the face opposite to the one having 5.
questions.questionHtml: Six numbers 5, 3, 6, 7, 9 and 2 are written on different faces of a dice. Two positions of this dice are shown in the figure below. Find the number on the face opposite to the one having 5.
questions.solution:
From both dices, 3 is common and on the same surface. So, all remaining surface will be opposite to each other.

So, 2 will be opposite to 5.

questions.question: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘÷’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged? 7 + 4 ÷ 18 – 3 × 2 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘÷’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged?
7 + 4 ÷ 18 – 3 × 2 = ?
questions.solution:
After interchanging the signs then:

⇒ 7 × 4 - 18 ÷ 3 + 2 = ? ⇒ ? = 7 × 4 - 6 + 2 ⇒ ? = 28 - 6 + 2 ⇒ ? = 30 - 6 = 24
